note: 13 measured regions over 10 pages; 9 figure rows and 3 non-exhibit regions plus one plate-panel fragment excluded, unaccounted 0. The paper prints no table caption and no table number anywhere in its 24 pages, yet it prints two unnumbered result grids (p14, 28 data rows of [T,N,E] against final USD with the last row printing no index, and p15, 4 rows of [gold fee, bitcoin fee] against final USD). Neither grid was boxed by the measurer - they are text-layer rows under a header line with no rules - so neither can be a row here and both are declared in the study note. The paragraph on p14 calls its grid 'the table below' and the paragraph on p15 calls its grid 'accompanying chart', so the paper names the object two different ways and numbers it neither. Caption side for all nine figures was settled from PyMuPDF word coordinates against the measured bbox, not from block order: Figure 1's group caption sits between the two panel regions and below them, Figure 2's below its plate, and the remaining seven below their plates. Section paths are overridden on p7, p9, p13, p15 and p16: the layout pass filed the p7 plates under '2 Analysis of the Problem' with kind result (the section is a problem analysis, not a result), the p9 flow chart under a welded '3 Calculating and Simplifying the Model 5' plus 3.5 Extreme Market Conditions (the plate prints above 3.4 Selling), Figure 5 under 4.3 Parameter Optimization (it belongs to 4.2 Weight Factor), Figure 7 under 4.4 with kind model (a fee sweep is a sensitivity), and Figure 8 under 5.2 Gold Buy/Sell (it is the bitcoin plate of 5.1). The build quotes whole printed lines, so several lead and trail quotes begin or end mid-clause; Figure 2's post-plate reading sentence is declared here because both its printed lines start mid-clause (one under the date fragment '9/10/2021.', the next under 'difference in scale'), so it is not recorded as a quote: 'Although the movement appears to be connected, figure 2 shows that the difference in scale is drastic.'
rules: All nine figure captions print BELOW their artwork and none above; the paper contains no table caption at all, so the side rule here is a figure-only rule [caption.position].
Every caption is a bare noun phrase or a participle phrase - zero finite verbs, zero units, zero conclusions - so voice is 'none' on all nine rows [caption.voice] [caption.concludes] [caption.units].
Three captions name a plotted window (9/11/2016-9/10/2021, 1610-1760 days, 460-560 days) and those are the only captions that carry a condition; the rest name only the object [caption.conditions].

One paper, two caption levels: Figure 1 is the only plate with lettered sub-captions ('1a:', '1b:') under each panel plus a parent caption for the pair, and both levels sit below their artwork [caption.numbering] [caption.verbatim].

Figures 6 and 7 carry word-for-word identical captions ('Results under different combinations.'), so a caption is not an identifier for this paper - page and number are [caption.verbatim] [caption.numbering].

One plate template carries the whole results chapter: Figures 4, 6 and 7 are the same indice-keyed portfolio curve on the same day axis, differing in series count (4 solid, 27 dashed, 4 solid) and in what the indices mean [geometry.family] [geometry.panel_layout].

Colour without a key: Figures 8 and 9 draw buys and sells as red and blue stems with no legend, and the only statement of the colour code is the caption plus one body sentence [geometry.legend] [caption.verbatim].

Legends, where they exist, are always inside the axes at upper left - five of nine rows - and are numbered rather than named on Figures 6 and 7, forcing the reader into the adjacent grid for the parameter set [geometry.legend].

No colour bar, no three-dimensional plate, no heatmap, no scatter, no photograph anywhere in the paper, and no plate prints data values on the artwork; every number the prose quotes is carried by the text or by the unnumbered grids [geometry.colorbar] [geometry.three_d] [geometry.printed_numbers] [geometry.data_labels].
Only the flow chart (Figure 3) has a true panel-free diagram layout with its labels inside the nodes; it is also the only non-chart artwork outside the memo [geometry.family] [geometry.legend].

Pointing is subject-first: five rows are launched by 'Figure N shows/describes/is' and three more by a locative 'as shown in' / 'seen in' clause; only Figure 5 is pointed at with a bare copula ('Figure 5 is the effect ...') [mention.lead_pattern] [mention.style].

The pointing case is inconsistent inside one paper ('Figure 3', 'Figure 5', 'Figure 9' against 'figure 2', 'figure 4', 'figure 6', 'figure 7', 'figure 8'), and three of the nine are pointed at only through their sub-panel letters ('figure 1a', 'Figures 1a and 1b') [mention.style].

Exhibits are cited after the fact as often as before it: Figures 6 and 7 are first cited on a later page than they print, while Figures 3 and 9 are announced a page early - in this paper the pointer lands wherever the paragraph happens to be, not beside the plate [mention.first_page] [mention.lead_pages] [mention.trail_sentence].

Reading sentences are formulaic and locative when present ('Observing figure 4 and comparing figure 1a and 1b we can see that ...', 'Observing the active orders from figure 8, we can see that ...', 'Figure 9 shows the buy times, but not the amounts.'), and the flow chart is the one plate whose reading sentence is its announcing sentence [mention.trail_sentence] [mention.read_sentences].

A result grid is written as a page of rows under a header line, with no table number, no caption, no rules and no page reference of its own: the p14 grid is called 'the table below' and the p15 grid is called 'accompanying chart' in the same paper [place.area_frac] [caption.verbatim].
